result:
I checked all 150 rules against the formula in their own docstrings and the module docstring. Nine of them behaved differently, and I fixed all nine:

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 40 | Used `qty > 5`, so 5 units got no discount | Changed to `qty >= 5` |
| 61, 89 | Whole rules computed the discount only on units above the threshold (marginal formula) | Changed to `base * 3 // 100` |
| 75, 125 | Capped the amount the percentage is applied to, not the discount itself | Compute the discount first, then cap it |
| 94 | Used `round(...)`, which can round up instead of flooring to the won | Changed to `// 100` |
| 136 | Used `qty >= 21`, so 20 units got no discount | Changed to `qty >= 20` |
| 149 | Applied the 50,000-won cap only when the discount was over 100,000 | Always apply `min(disc, 50000)` |
| 150 | Marginal rule discounted all units (whole formula) | Changed to `(qty - 100) * unit * 12 // 100` |

Some other rules are written differently, like `qty >= 6` in rule 02 and `qty > 100` in another marginal rule. They give the same results, because a marginal rule's discount at the threshold is 0 anyway, so I left them alone.

To check, I wrote a separate script that builds the expected price from each docstring. It compared that with every rule over 263 quantities and 15 unit prices, and also confirmed that negative inputs raise `ValueError`. Before the fixes it flagged exactly these nine rules; after the fixes, none.

STATUS: DONE
